I am 74 years old and I never spent one day in school. I cannot read or write. I have farmed this 2 mu of cotton for 55 years — my mother-in-law taught me when I first married into this family.

I don't listen to advice from outsiders. I listen to what Old Wang and my nephew do, because their fields are right next to mine and I can see if their cotton grows well. Last year I used the same seed they used — the new kind from the seed shop, not the old cotton my grandmother grew. It cost more but gave better cotton.

For fertilizer, I bought two bags of the compound kind, 50 kg each. One bag for each mu. I paid about 120 yuan per bag. The dealer says it has three numbers on it — 15, 15, 15. I don't know what those numbers mean exactly, but I know one bag per mu is what everyone puts down. I spread it before planting and then the rotary tiller man comes through. I don't buy any other fertilizer. Two bags is already 240 yuan, and my granddaughter needs money for school.

I water twice from our well. Once when the young plants look dry in early summer, and once in late summer when the cotton pods are swelling. Every time I run the pump, the electric meter spins and my husband yells about the bill. So two times is enough.

The cotton worms come every year. I spray medicine for them about 13 times from summer to fall. When I see holes in the leaves or worms on the buds, I mix the medicine and spray. I also spray once for weeds right after the cotton comes up. My daughter-in-law helps me carry the sprayer. We don't hire anyone — we can't afford it.

I think I will get about 500 kg of cotton per mu this year. Last year I got around that much. If I get less, my son who works in the city factory will send money. But I still don't want to waste fertilizer money, and I don't want to use too little and have the cotton look yellow and thin. One bag per mu feels safe. That's what my neighbors do.
